cells.tense: The weight is here now, and the hands stay on it while it finishes.
cells.act: carry on with the version you chose through another week of doubt
cells.ask: Take the thing you are already seeing through and give it seven more ordinary days. Follow the version you picked before the doubt showed up, planned work only, no hunting for a result. Either way the week reports.
cells.core:
Where something is closing out, you can stand under the weight of it and keep working — no bracing, no counting the days. A finish doesn't send you hunting for proof the effort was wasted. You let the last stretch stay plain.

An ending like this takes time to complete, and the work you already chose is how you sit through it. Give that one task another week of ordinary effort, no confirmation needed. Should it still hold, good; should it stop holding, next week's work says so plainly, and you'll have found it out by doing it rather than standing at the edge of it waiting.
cells.sheetLine: The load is real, and you can still work under it.
cells.place: where something is ending so something else can start

cells.tense: You will brace for the coming ending and pick up more of it than was set down.
cells.act: let the exchange with someone run both ways
cells.ask: Halfway through the next load you take on for somebody, stop and say you need a hand with the rest. Let them do their half. Then leave the step after that to them.
cells.core:
You hold, and right now you hold in advance of the thing itself — gripping an ending that hasn't arrived, bearing more of it than was handed to you. What used to steady a room stiffens before the pressure does, and a grip that tight leaves no room beside you for anyone to stand. Holding is meant to contain what's actually there.

Choose somebody you've been doing the heavy part for. Partway through, stop and ask plainly for help with the remainder. Take it, and leave them the piece that follows. No explanation needed, and you don't owe thanks for the hand you asked for. Watch how much less there is to keep braced against.
cells.sheetLine: You're bracing for an ending that hasn't happened yet.

cells.tense: Something ended, and you are still fixed at a doorway that is behind you now.
cells.act: accept the acknowledgment when it comes
cells.ask: Someone close has seen what you saw through to the end. When they mention it, or reach to take something off your hands, don't deflect. Let it stand, and take what comes back.
cells.core:
Pressure arrives now and your grip has loosened — the load shows up and something in you steps aside from it. Your attention stays back at the ending that's over. So the part that could carry weight is waiting at the wrong door.

What you did there got finished, and close enough that somebody saw it. That's the way back — not more effort. When the person it was for says what they noticed, or offers a hand with something small, stay for it and take what's given. Letting thanks land isn't the same as lying down under a load; it tells you the strength is still yours.
cells.sheetLine: You got through it and you're still at the old doorway.

cells.tense: You are already keeping things going through this ending while your own account says otherwise.
cells.act: go on toward it without needing a sign
cells.ask: You keep moving toward something. Pick it this week and write one line naming it on a scrap you'll see daily. Keep going as you were — no sign required.
cells.core:
Through an ending, the practical side keeps running — calls returned, dates kept, the day's version of the work done — and if you heard it described back, none of it would be down as yours. Things stay level because you keep them level. That survives whatever the account says.

There is a thing you've been quietly heading for the whole time this was ending. Write one line naming it on a scrap you'll pass each day, and keep moving the way you already have. Nothing needs to confirm the choice; you'll have the same forward motion you had, only now the scrap is the record you kept for yourself.
cells.sheetLine: You've been keeping it level and calling none of it yours.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim: that material difficulty has already tested this person's endurance; I only have the capacity and the seat, not their history. The reader could reasonably say no one in particular is asking them to hold anything, or that the ending in front of them is someone else's. The asks survive being wrong because each is one visible act, not a verdict on their life — if the read misses, finishing one thing still leaves them with a finished thing. The sentence that serves me rather than them: 'Strength found in what you carry, not what you're given' — it flatters the reader's craft instead of telling them anything they can use; struck from every cell.
